label: first copy step of length-3 sequences; weakly on l/i/n-like tokens at original positions 1-2
predicate: ((L == 3) & (t == 4)) | ((phase == 0) & (t >= 1) & (t <= 2) & ((in_tok == tok("l")) | (isin(in_tok, [tok("i"), tok("n"), tok("s"), tok("w"), tok("z")]) & isin(prev_tok, [tok("t"), tok("k"), tok("v"), tok("j")]))))
explanation: Two regimes. (1) Strong: in L=3 sequences at t=4, the step after <DEL> where the model outputs original token 1. This fires ~96% of the time and holds ~55% of activation mass, including nearly all of the top quartile; every top example is like "l q h <DEL> [l] q". (2) Weak, token-dependent: original-phase steps t=1 and t=2 whose input is l (the strongest token, 12x lift) or i/n/s/w/z, more likely after t/k/v/j. These are mostly low/mid-quartile activations. It never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, at t>=6, or in copy steps of L>=4 sequences other than recall_idx 1-2. Precision in regime 2 is limited (many l at t=1-2 are inactive), so this is token-pair-specific rather than clean.
